To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MSSS and MSSS2 problems are solvable in polynomial-time for quasi-transitive and for all digraph classes that can be obtained by replacing the vertices of strong semicomplete (and some other classes of) digraphs with digraphs whose minimum path covering number can also be decided in polynomial-time.
the MSSS is solvable in quasi-transitive and in extended semiconplete digraphs.

the problem of finding the MSSS in quasi-transitive and in some other digraphs is polynomially solv- able and that it is solvable in quasi-polynomial time for digraphs whose arc set can be partitioned into strongly connected digraphs whose size is polynomially bounded in the size of the original digraph.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new problem in graph theory and with new results on the structure of digraphs.
strongly connected spanning subgraphs in digraphs that have some additional structure.
the problem of finding an MSSS in quasi-transitive and extended semicomplete (and some more general) digraphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MSSS-problem is polynomially soluble for all digraph classes for which the path covering number of the digraphs in the class can be decided in a polynomial time.

the MSSS is solvable in time polynomial in the number of arcs for digraphs that are either quasi-transitive or can be obtained from a strong semicomplete graph on at least two nodes by replacing each vertex by a digraph with a polynomially decidable path covering number.

the MSSS is solvable in linear time for digraphs that are either quasi-transitive or can be obtained from a strong semicomplete by replacing some of its vertices with digraphs whose arc set can be computed in polynomial time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MSSS-problem is polynomially soluble for all digraph classes that are defined by forbidden subdigraphs and that can be obtained by replacing each vertex of strong semicomplete (or strong semicomplete bipartite) digraphs with an arbitrary digraph belonging to the class of digraphs with bounded path covering number.
the MSSS is solvable in time O(n^3m) for all quasi-transitive digaphs and for all digraph that can be obtained by the above-mentioned construction from strong semicompete digraphs.

the MSSS-problem is solvable in quasi-transitive and extended semicomplete (strong) digraphs, and in digraphs obtained from strong semiconplete digraphs by replacing some vertices with digraphs whose MSSS-problem can be solved in polynomial time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the path covering number of a digraph is a useful tool for studying the MSSS problem in digraphs.
the structure of cycles in quasi-transitive (and extended semicomplete) digraphs is very similar to the structure of cycles of the underlying undirected graphs.
a polynomial-time algorithm can be designed for the MSSS problem if the path covering number of the digraph is polynomial-time decidable.
